title: Constant-scalar bilinearity of the normalized integral completed tensor

from.place: The assigned integral-to-rational tensor construction needs separate linearity of the integral arrow action before applying module base change. The assigned Lean definitions retain the normalized finite-reduction/Roos model.

statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l with valuation ring O_E [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme W. Let T be the normalized ambient integralCompletedTensor of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], on the derived category of modules over the completed coefficient sheaf, equipped with the published constant O_E action [lem-weil-integral-constructible-linear]. For any four ambient derived objects M, M′, N, N′, there is an O_E-bilinear map Hom(M,M′) x Hom(N,N′) -> Hom(T(M,N),T(M′,N′)) whose value on (a,b) is exactly T.map(a,b). No completeness, constructibility, boundedness, flatness or geometric hypothesis on the objects or scheme is imposed.

source.place: Flat resolutions, lemma-K-flat-resolution (Tag 06YS), derived tensor construction following lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side; normalized finite-reduction/Roos construction of def-pur-integral-derived-operations and lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined. Constant-scalar calculation written by G2.

proof.text: Use the canonical constant-section module action on completed coefficient sheaves. Map its section ring homomorphism through the finite coefficient projection. The existing reduction_action identity identifies scalar multiplication after reduction with this projected action. Restriction of scalars is linear for these two actions. On the sheafified finite tensor, test the map on pure tensors through the sheafification adjunction: (a f)(x) tensor y = a (f(x) tensor y). The symmetric braiding gives the other variable. The existing additive and linear total-bifunctor constructions extend these equations to complexes, including the signed total differential.

Evaluate a morphism of strict tensor towers at each finite index. The preceding separate additivity and scalar identities hold at every index, so natural-transformation extensionality proves them on the towers. Compose with the proved additive and linear Roos functor: its product map and its two mapping-cone components preserve addition and scalars. The scalar comparison for the published derived action identifies the canonical Q functor as linear. Hence the tensor model on good representatives is separately additive and linear.

The good-complex inclusion followed by Q is a localization at quasi-isomorphisms, using K-flat resolutions, and its source has binary biproducts. Fix one good representative and restrict integralCompletedTensorComparison to the other variable. This is a natural isomorphism from the composite of localization and the corresponding partial descended tensor to the partial good model. Additivity descends via preservation of binary products and zero maps; linearity descends by Localization.functor_linear_iff. Essential surjectivity of good localization and the partial tensor functor applied to a representative isomorphism then give additivity and linearity with any ambient object fixed. Apply this argument in both variables.

Define the bilinear Hom map by first mapping the first arrow with the second source object fixed, then mapping the second arrow with the first target object fixed, and composing. The partial-functor equations and bilinearity of composition prove the four linear-map laws. Functoriality and (a,id) followed by (id,b) = (a,b) identify its value with integralCompletedTensor.map. These constructions use no cancellation and include zero objects, zero arrows, and arbitrary torsion.

mathlib_searches.query: Derived tensor product of sheaves of modules is linear in each morphism argument
mathlib_searches.results: TensorProduct.map and PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorHom_app describe the ordinary tensor; CategoryTheory.tensorRight_linear needs a linear monoidal structure. None supplies separate linearity for this normalized completed derived tensor.

mathlib_searches.query: Extend a bilinear functor to scalar localization by tensoring morphisms
mathlib_searches.results: CategoryTheory.Localization.linear and functor_linear_iff, Localization.Monoidal.tensorBifunctor and IsLocalizedModule.map_lTensor. These do not give integralCompletedTensor bilinearity.
TensorProduct.curry, curry_apply and curry_injective, used for the proved scalar-extension step in the parent, not for this integral bilinearity.

No integralCompletedTensor bilinearity theorem. DerivedCompletedTensorBilinearity uses a different reflector-based model. CompletedTensorScalarLinearity proves first-variable scalar preservation on constructibles but imports the parent, so cannot supply this prerequisite without a cycle; it does not state separate additivity and second-variable scalar preservation. IntegralDerivedHomBilinear is for Hom, not tensor. Searched lean/WeilConjectures and lean/Sheaf plus Mathlib via msearch.

lean.statement:
theorem integralCompletedTensor_bilinear (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (W : Scheme.{u})
    (M M' N N' : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l E W)) :
    ∃ b : (M ⟶ M') →ₗ[Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E]
        (N ⟶ N') →ₗ[Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E]
        ((integralCompletedTensor l E W).obj (M, N) ⟶
          (integralCompletedTensor l E W).obj (M', N')),
      ∀ a b', b a b' = (integralCompletedTensor l E W).map (Prod.mkHom a b')
